items.title: Wilson "Willie T" Turbinton Interview, 1990-09
items.q: I know that there were people, big name musicians, Cannonball Adderley for one, Joe Zawinil for another, who were interested in what you were doing and were here. ... I can remember meeting all those people in the workshop.

ctx.x: It just depends on the setting. I can play everything from the Little Richards to whatever is fusion to all of that. And I think to a large degree that that has been our problem. People having record companies sometimes want you to have, to market you, they want you to record in one mode. And you know I know personally I can sing, I can sing jazz, I can sing rock and roll, or whatever. And when you're promoting yourself no one wants to hear you blow your horn. And since I've come to that realization I sometimes…

Speaking of marketing, would you talk a little bit about the workshop? And I know that there were people, big name musicians, Cannonball Adderley for one, Joe Zawinil for another, who were interested in what you were doing and were here. Would you talk a little bit about that?

Well, fortunately at the time that the workshop happened, Al Hurd had a club on Bourbon Street that featured a lot of the name acts. And when serious musicians come to town, they kind of look for the places to go to hear differently. And we had gotten a pretty good reputation as jazz players. And you know, Freddie Hubbard's just about Jimmy Smith. I can remember meeting all those people in the workshop. And I mean, their main reason for being in this city was them being employed over at Al Hurd's. And then I can…
